item.title: Best performers from 49ers' shootout win vs. Cowboys
item.description: The San Francisco 49ers traveled south to take on the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Sunday for a battle between non-division NFC rivals, and Kyle Shanahan's team earned a 46-40 win, moving to 8-1 on the year. San Francisco's offense played very well, while the defense left a lot to be desired, but it was enough to drop the Cowboys to 4-6. As we continue to comb through this victory, let's take a look at some of San Francisco's top performers from this Week 10 matchup. QB Brock Purdy Purdy played an incredible game despite being under constant pressure and taking five sacks. He completed 78.6% of his passes for 389 yards and three touchdowns while rushing for another 21 yards on two scrambles. This looked like the performance of a potential MVP. RB Christian McCaffrey Sunday was one of the best games of McCaffrey's career. He rushed for 62 yards and a touchdown on 4.8 yards per attempt, but he was even more effective as a pass catcher, hauling in all four of his targets for 161 yards and two touchdowns. Not being forced to be the bell cow this year has really helped him this year. RB Kaelon Black Spelling McCaffrey a lot this year, Black has played really well in his rookie year. Against the Cowboys, he ran for 53 yards and a touchdown on 4.8 yards per attempt. His 25-yard score was incredible, as he ran over two defenders on his way to the end zone. Black also caught two passes for 13 yards. WR Deebo Samuel Samuel made his return to the field this week after missing time due to an injury. He caught three passes for 31 yards, including an 11-yard touchdown. He also carried the ball three times for 78 yards, including a 70-yard score on a reverse. Samuel brings a different dimension to this offseason when he's healthy. item.title: Are 49ers due for a reality check? Red flags emerged in wild win over Cowboys
item.description: San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy, bottom, is sacked by Dallas Cowboys defensive tackle LT Overton during the first half on Sunday in Arlington, Texas. (Tony Gutierrez/Associated Press) The San Francisco 49ers second travelogue trip of the season got off to an exciting start on Sunday, surviving a wild - and somewhat alarming - shootout with the Dallas Cowboys, 46-40. Now they head from the plains of Texas to the Rocky Mountains and then take a hard left to go south of the border to Mexico City, during their second lengthy, multi-country trip. The good news is the 49ers are tied for a league best 8-1. The better news - for the coaches - is that, during this long week away from home, the 49ers have plenty to keep them occupied. Like tightening up that problematic defense. Improving the pass rush. And keeping Brock Purdy upright. Twelve days after Democrats turned Texas blue, 49ers fans turned Dallas red, taking over AT&T Stadium and making Jerry Jones' palace sound like their home stadium. For the fans' next trick, they'll try to turn Mexico red. "Our fans are awesome," head coach Kyle Shanahan said. "Wish I could give them all game balls." The 49ers have cruised to an 8-1 record, and the most impressive part of the first half of the season has been vanquishing their most heated rivals away from their home stadium: the Rams in Australia, the Seahawks in Seattle and, on Sunday, the Cowboys, in Arlington, Texas. But the upcoming second half of the season holds some potential concerns. And Sunday's split personality game underscored those worries. "It was sort of a weird game," Purdy said. While the 49ers offense looked like the most elite on the planet on Sunday, racking up 584 yards, the 49ers defense couldn't say the same thing. The 49ers swamped the Cowboys from the end of the second quarter until early in the fourth quarter, outscoring Dallas 28-3 in that stretch. But then the 49ers found themselves in an uncomfortably tight situation, giving up three Dallas touchdowns in the final 9:08 of the game and having to survive an onside kick, their own fumble (that they recovered), a three-and-out and a Dallas attempt at a Cal Bears-style lateral-fest comeback. "Anytime you get 40 dropped on you, you're going to be upset," said linebacker Fred Warner . "You've got to look at the tape and see why that was the case." There will be a lot of tape to watch in the coming week, while getting acclimated to altitude in Colorado Springs. Though the first half of the season has gone almost perfectly, there is still a long road ahead. Next week, in Estadio Azteca, the 49ers will face Minnesota, a team that - unlike the Cowboys - will present a ferocious defense. And, with the addition of Kirk Cousins, a team that suddenly looks like a true Super Bowl contender. Trouncing the Arkansas-Pine Bluff Golden Lions 122-46, the squad improved to 4-0 on the season to open up a three-game homestand. The 76-point victory marked the largest margin of victory in program history. The victory also marks the seventh time in head coach Eric Musselman's career that his teams have started the season with four consecutive wins. Sunday showcased a wire-to-wire, well-rounded effort led by a dominant performance from forward Adonis Ratliff. "I feel like today it was easy to show off my playmaking," Ratliff said. "I feel like I'm a pretty good passer. I don't get to show it much, but I feel like I was able to do that today." It was an Adonis avalanche from the beginning, as the freshman got the Trojans out to an 8-0 advantage all by himself. He put back a missed attempt from his brother Darius before drilling back-to-back triples and forcing an early timeout from the Golden Lions. Adonis continued to fill up the stat sheet in more ways than one, making his presence felt just as strongly on the defensive end of the floor. By the end of the afternoon, he compiled 17 points to go along with eight rebounds, five assists and four blocks. item.title: Joe Flacco replaces Joe Burrow in 4th quarter of Bengals-Steelers rout
item.description: Cincinnati Bengals backup quarterback Joe Flacco entered in the fourth quarter of the team's NFL Week 10 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium on NBC's Sunday Night Football , as the Bengals sat starter Joe Burrow with a 38-18 lead. Burrow left the game having completed 35-of-44 for 409 passing yards with four touchdowns. He had 302 passing yards in the first half . When Flacco started for the Bengals in 2025 against Aaron Rodgers, ESPN Research reported that it was the second time in NFL history that two quarterbacks at least 40 years old face off in a regular-season or postseason game. The Steelers' Cam Heyward dubbed it the "Icy Hot" Bowl . Rodgers is the only active NFL quarterback older than Flacco. Rodgers' announcement in May that he'll retire after the 2026 season means the Bengals may not face the future Pro Football Hall of Famer again. Flacco got to enter the team's NFL Week 7 rout of the Ravens in Baltimore during the fourth quarter and finish the game against his former team, but he did not attempt a pass. Flacco entered Week 7 having appeared in one game for the Bengals this season but without attempting a pass. Flacco told Burrow he thought Burrow's first touchdown pass to Ja'Marr Chase against the Houston Texans was "uncatchable." Rodgers' announcement in May that he'll retire after the 2026 season means the Bengals may not face the future Pro Football Hall of Famer again. Flacco, who turned 41 in January, played in nine games last season for the Bengals , making six starts after Burrow suffered a turf toe injury during a Week 2 win against Jacksonville . Flacco completed 158 of 254 pass attempts for 1,664 yards with 13 touchdowns. In November 2025, Flacco played with a sprained AC joint in his throwing shoulder during a 47-42 loss to the Chicago Bears . At 40 years old, Flacco became the oldest quarterback in NFL history to pass for 470 yards in a game. item.title: Bucks coach Taylor Jenkins tinkers with starting lineups as losses pile up
item.description: In an ever-lengthening quest for a single win – and the consistency needed for 48 minutes to capture a victory – Milwaukee Bucks head coach Taylor Jenkins tried his fifth different starting lineup in five games in a 113-106 loss to Atlanta on Nov. 15 as Jericho Sims joined the opening unit. Some of that change was due to injury, as Tyler Herro missed the game in New York on Nov. 11 with injury and Ousmane Dieng, who started in Orlando on Nov. 13, broke his finger in that game. But it’s possible Jenkins would’ve tinkered anyway against the Hawks, as he came into the game having put together 150 different five-man combinations despite having arguably the league’s healthiest team. Now, not all those lineups logged major minutes – there were just six who played at least 15 or more together – but it’s been part of an intentional fact-gathering start to the year for Jenkins as he tries to identify who the next group of winning Bucks players are. “We’re not driven by necessarily the wins and losses,” Jenkins said before the game against Atlanta. “It’s the process. Like, how are those units actually playing together? Where are the leads being built, where they’re being lost? How’s our offense functioning, defense functioning? "So, still sorting through that right now but hopefully sooner rather than later.” BOX SCORE: Hawks 113, Bucks 106 The issue is the current iteration of the Bucks are not winning now – they have now lost 10 straight games and are 1-13 on the season – which has created an inherent tension of having an urgency to win vs. playing the very necessary long game of development. “It’s definitely the psychological situation right now,” Jenkins acknowledged. “Is the winning shouldn’t just validate the process, our process of how we’re developing. Chase and Tee Higgins celebrated Chase's first-quarter TD with a bullfighting nod . item.title: Cowboys Make Unwanted History in Wild Loss to 49ers
item.description: Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker's unit had a rough go of things on Sunday. Getty When San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey gashed the Dallas Cowboys for a third touchdown on Sunday, America’s Team endured a most-unwanted record. Dallas gave up a franchise home record 584 yards in a 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday in Week 10. The Cowboys kept things close in the first half, down 17-16 at the half, but the Dallas defense melted against the 49ers skill players, especially McCaffrey. Things started downhill defensively for the Cowboys in the second half when 49ers running back Kaelon Black scored on a 25-yard touchdown run for 24-16 lead. Dallas then gave up a 70-yard touchdown run by 49ers wide receiver Deebo Samuel, and McCaffrey added touchdowns of 16 yards and 66 yards. Cowboys Offense Caught On Too Late Dallas only managed a field goal in the third quarter, but Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott and company found a rhythm in the fourth quarter. Prescott led the Cowboys six plays and 65 yards on a scoring drive, capped by wide receiver George Pickens’ 5-yard touchdown catch. That cut the Niners lead to 38-25, and the Cowboys scored again, 38-32, when Prescott connected with wide receiver Ryan Flournoy for 11 yards. Dallas then answered McCaffrey’s 66-yard score with a 12-play, 76-yard scoring drive in 2:40. Prescott hit wide receiver CeeDee Lamb for 1-yard touchdown to trim the 49ers lead to 46-40 with 43 seconds left. The Cowboys’ last-gasp lateral attempt then fell short amid a big home loss on national TV. Dallas Defense Wastes 5-Sack Day The Cowboys sacked 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy five times on Sunday, but that did little in the end. Quinnen Williams, who also had nine tackles, sacked Purdy once, as did Elijah Garcia, who had five tackles. James Houston and Otito Ogbonnia each had a half sack, and LT Overton had a sack as did Jonathan Bullard. While that was a disappointment for the Cowboys with record yardage allowed, Dallas at least avoided giving up more than the franchise record of 54 points from 1970. item.title: Rondout Valley secures first state field hockey championship
item.description: Years of contending finally resulted in a state championship for Rondout Valley field hockey on Sunday, Nov. 15. The Ganders completed a 20-0 season by knocking off five-time defending state champion Whitney Point in the state Class C title match in Freedom Plains. A goal scored by Madison Shanley just 1:47 into the match was all that was needed. Rondout had lost to Whitney Point in the final the past two seasons, including a 3-2 overtime setback in 2025. "This team is special,'' said Rondout coach Nanette Simione, believing "third time's a charm.'' More: Section 9 field hockey scores, schedule for the 2026 season "They have worked tirelessly not just this season but all off-season since last year. ... The team knew what it would take and we prepared for this every day this season. "We played smart, supported one another all game, passed well, played great team defense, had great defensive corners and, most of all, never let down for 60 minutes.'' A penalty occurred just outside the penalty circle. Audrey Dennin began the re-start from the apex, delivering a short pass to Ella Morse on the left side. She deftly sidestepped a charging Kylan Smith, dribbled a short distance and slapped a back-handed, diagonal shot from 15 yards out toward the right goal post. Just before the shot, Shanley broke toward the post and past defender Grace Lewis, getting her stick down for the deflection, with goalkeeper Lauren Magill off her line. "Scoring so early in the game gave us momentum and confidence to work every second to make this happen,'' Simione said. "Right down to the last play, when Ella Morse stopped their corner attempt and cleared it out, we never gave up.'' Morgan Bresnahan, who was hardly challenged all season due to Rondout's suffocating defense, made seven stops for the shutout. Whitney Point finished at 18-2-1. The Eagles had won 10 state titles since 1984. In Saturday's semifinals, Rondout rolled past Greenwich 4-1. Samantha Schneller scored two of her three goals in the opening four minutes and Madison Shanley scored midway through the third quarter. Simone praised the defensive work of Addison O'Donnell, Stella Greco and Cierra Miller. Morse, Dennin and Ella Schoonmaker were chosen to the all-tournament team. Addison O'Donnell was the team's winner of the sportsmanship award from the state association. "So many past players have reached out after this win,'' Simione said. "Their hard work over the years was pivotal in creating the culture for Rondout Valley field hockey. These girls continued that and finally brought home the state championship. For now, we plan to take this all in and enjoy this experience.'' In addition to the past two seasons, Rondout lost in the 2008 state final and 2021 semifinals. Although she was accustomed to competing at higher weights, the UFC’s highest women’s division was featherweight at 145lbs. As a result, Harrison had little choice but to shed another 20lbs to compete at bantamweight. The weight cut has taken its toll, and considering her growing list of injuries, fans may never see her compete at 135lbs again. However, the possibility of a rematch with Nunes at featherweight remains on the table. During the UFC 334 post-fight press conference , Harrison expressed her interest in moving up to 145lbs, saying, “(Nunes rematch at) 145. I’ve got to go get that other belt. I don’t want to speak quickly; I’m going to go back. I’m going to talk to my team. I’m going to take some time and be with my kids.” Harrison also discussed another potential dream matchup, this time against former UFC women’s bantamweight champion Ronda Rousey. She said, “I get to have the holidays with my kids and actually eat and not be sweaty or hungry or grumpy. Then, we’ll see what happens. If Ronda (Rousey) wants to come get some, it would be fun. Free money.” While Nunes appeared to be back in competition full-time, judging by her post-UFC 334 reaction, a matchup with Rousey could be more difficult to materialize. The former UFC champion made her MMA return outside the promotion against Gina Carano, headlining MVP MMA 1 in May 2026. The two have a history dating back nearly 20 years, when they were both Olympic hopefuls training at Jimmy Pedro’s Judo Center. Rousey was three years older than Harrison and was the more established judoka at the time. She defeated Harrison on both occasions they competed against each other. However, Harrison would eventually come out on top on the Olympic stage. While Rousey won a bronze medal at the 2008 Olympics, Harrison claimed gold at the 2012 and 2016 Games.

item.title: 49ers radio announcer loses his voice during record-setting win vs. Cowboys
item.description: George Kittle celebrates with Christian McCaffrey of the San Francisco 49ers after McCaffrey scored a fourth quarter touchdown against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Nov. 15, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Stacy Revere/Getty Images) How banged up are the San Francisco 49ers ? Even their radio play-by-play announcer Guy Haberman was not at 100% on Sunday. Haberman lost his voice during the Niners' 46-40 win over the Cowboys in Arlington, Texas, though he was able to complete the broadcast. Signs that Haberman was under the weather were evident when SFGATE listened to the pregame show on KNBR, as Haberman was speaking noticeably softer than he typically does. As he called the high-scoring game that featured a bevy of long touchdowns, Haberman wasn't able to get to the usual octave levels and excitement that he brings when he calls 49ers touchdowns and big moments. Haberman's voice started to crack at the end of the 74-yard touchdown pass that Brock Purdy threw to Christian McCaffrey in the first half. It was a similar tone in the second half on Deebo Samuel's 70-yard touchdown run on a reverse, with multiple blocks downfield from Purdy and Trent Williams. Haberman's voice cracked as he gave his big "Touchdown 49ers" call and sounded audibly under the weather. "A 70-yard reverse! With Purdy out in front blocking!" "This one's for Papa: Deebo does Dallas for a second time!" Haberman and T-Rock with some 📻🔥 https://t.co/2uZK83MBGR - KNBR (@KNBR) November 15, 2026 Late in the fourth quarter, right after another long McCaffrey touchdown put the final touch on the win over Dallas, analyst Tim Ryan openly acknowledged Haberman's voice struggles on air. "How much do you have left in that voice?" Ryan asked Haberman. The play-by-play man replied, "3:23," matching the amount of time that was left in the game. Haberman is serving as the Niners' primary fill-in for Greg Papa , who has missed most of the last two seasons with a variety of health concerns , including cancer, a bone marrow transplant and lung failure. Papa was hoping to return to the booth this season, but he was hospitalized right before the season began with heart issues. While the 49ers mostly used Haberman to fill Papa's seat last year, Haberman had commitments that led the team to use four other play-by-play broadcasters to fill in for other games. The 49ers haven't officially acknowlegded hiring Haberman full-time, but the team clearly had Haberman set to be in position to work every 49ers game. Had Papa been able to broadcast games, Haberman was set to shift to being a sideline reporter on the broadcast. He's also hosting a weekly interview series called " The 49ers Guy " on the team's official YouTube channel . Papa famously lost his voice while calling a 49ers playoff game against the Packers in 2022, but was able to finish the game.
